title: The real lot: 215-16 Northern Boulevard, Queens (BBL 4073340070)
summary: An independent, by-hand reading of the R6B zoning limits for one real lot, 215-16 Northern Boulevard in Queens (BBL 4073340070). A C2-2 commercial overlay is recorded; the overlay's own rules are not read here. Every value below comes from the law text and the lot's recorded facts, never from a program run.
what_it_is_worth: Prepared by an AI helper and recomputed by a second AI; their agreement alone is not proof. It is a draft reading of the law, not professionally reviewed, and is not a statement that anything complies. It is one lot. Most sections were read from the same captures the rules were written from, so an error in a capture would be shared; four sections (ZR 23-22, 23-432, 23-362 and 23-52) were also read on the official page on 2026-10-06. The corner-lot definition it uses (ZR 12-10) and ZR 23-342 are now captured (task M4-T025) and were read independently by two step-P1 readings (see cases/step-p1-worked.json).
what_it_does_not_establish: It does not read the C2-2 commercial overlay; every residential figure here is the residential reading only. The overlay is read independently in cases/overlay-reading.json, where both step-P2 readings find it changes only the street-wall location rule and leaves the floor area ratio, lot coverage, dwelling units, base and building heights, the setback and the all-residential rear yard the same as plain R6B; no value in this case changes.
It does not prove the zoning lot; it is a tax-lot-only reading.
It does not settle lot coverage, the rear yard beyond the corner area, the ordinary rear-yard depth, or any building massing.
It is not a professional or legal determination and does not say the lot complies with anything.
prepared_by: An AI helper that took no part in writing the program's rules, working only from a sealed folder of pinned law-text captures and the lot's recorded facts, with no access to the program.
checked_by: A second AI recomputed the arithmetic and the geometry independently from the same sealed folder. Agreement between two AI answers alone is not proof.
sources: The independent hand-calculation, follow-up (tables C and D): provenance/return-independent-hand-calculation-2.md

The two step-P1 readings that confirm the corner, coverage and rear-yard rows from the newly captured text: provenance/return-independent-hand-calculation-3.md and provenance/return-independent-hand-calculation-4.md.
The sealed folder given to the helper: the pinned ZR captures (without the notes describing how the program encoded them) and the lot's recorded official facts, with no program access.
The law captures under docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/, each pinned by its content digest.

The helper's return (Task 1(g)) and the work order's independent value both give 35; the 'not known' sits in the program's first-screen column, which these cases do not copy. Reason: newly captured text.

Row L12 (rear yard): expected value unchanged (not known). ZR 23-342 is now captured (task M4-T025); a captured ZR 23-342 citation is added and the reason records that both step-P1 readings read no rear yard within 100 feet of the corner (ZR 23-344(a)) and the beyond-100-feet outcome and its depth as not known. Row L14 (ordinary rear-yard depth): expected value unchanged (not known). ZR 23-342 is now captured (task M4-T025), so the citation changes from not-captured to the captured snapshot zr-23-342; the reason now records that the depth ZR 23-342 sets depends on the building type and lot width, which are not given, so the depth for this lot is still not known. Reason: newly captured text.

No expected value changed. The C2-2 overlay has now been read independently in step P2 (task M4-T028, cases/overlay-reading.json); the first 'does not establish' item is extended to point to that reading, which finds the overlay changes only the street-wall location rule and leaves the floor area ratio, lot coverage, dwelling units, base and building heights, the setback and the all-residential rear yard the same as plain R6B. Both step-P2 readings support this. No row value changes; in particular row L5 (lot coverage) stays not known for its per-portion reason. citations.title: Maximum lot coverage in R6 through R12 Districts
citations.quote: the maximum residential lot coverage for interior lots or through lots shall be 80 percent and the maximum residential lot coverage for corner lots shall be 100 percent

citations.title: Definitions (lot, corner)
citations.quote: that portion bounded by the intersecting #street line# and lines parallel to and 100 feet from each intersecting #street line#

rows.why_applies: ZR 23-362(a) gives corner lots 100 percent and interior or through lots 80 percent; the captured ZR 12-10 corner-lot definition limits the 100-percent corner-lot rule to the portion within 100 feet of each street line. Part of this lot lies beyond 100 feet of the 215 Place street line, so it is a corner-lot portion plus a remaining interior-lot portion.

expected.reason: No single whole-lot coverage figure. The corner-lot 100-percent rule covers only the part of the lot within 100 feet of each street line; this lot reaches 103.93 feet from the 215 Place street line (a strip about 3.93 feet wide, about 390 square feet), so the whole lot is not the corner-lot portion. Both step-P1 readings read it per portion: the corner-lot portion has a maximum residential lot coverage of 100 percent and the remaining interior-lot portion 80 percent.

rows.source_reference: return-independent-hand-calculation-1.md, Task 1(e), and return-independent-hand-calculation-2.md, Q1(a)-(b); the per-portion reading is confirmed by both step-P1 readings (return-independent-hand-calculation-3.md and -4.md, Q2a).
rows.does_not_establish: It gives no whole-lot coverage percentage and does not settle the corner-lot portion to the square foot (the two step-P1 readings give about 9,998 and 9,997.6 square feet for the corner portion, resting on the approximate outline and a one-foot street-line tolerance).

citations.title: Additional rear yard modifications
citations.quote: no rear yard shall be required within 100 feet of the point of intersection of two street lines intersecting at an angle of 135 degrees or less

citations.title: Rear yard requirements
citations.quote: shall be provided on #interior lots# in accordance with this Section

rows.why_applies: ZR 23-344(a) requires no rear yard within 100 feet of the point where two street lines meet at 135 degrees or less (here 89.7 degrees); that waiver covers only the area within 100 feet of the corner point. ZR 23-342 requires a rear yard only on the interior-lot portion, and part of this lot lies beyond 100 feet of the corner, so what is required there is not settled by the captured text.

expected.reason: Within 100 feet of the corner point no rear yard is required (ZR 23-344(a)); but the far corner of the lot is 144.60 feet from the corner point, so part of the lot lies beyond that 100-foot reach, and whether a rear yard is required there is not settled. ZR 23-342 is now captured, but the depth it sets depends on the building type and lot width (not given); the first and step-P1 readers did not have the ZR 12-10 side- and rear-lot-line definitions, and both step-P1 readings read it the same way (no rear yard within 100 feet of the corner; beyond, not known). Those definitions were since captured (task M4-T029) and read in step P3 (cases/step-p3-worked.json), where both step-P3 readings again read the beyond-100-foot rear yard as not known (it needs the adjoining lot-line type and the building type, height and lot width, and the overlay yard rule ZR 34-23 was not available).

rows.source_reference: return-independent-hand-calculation-1.md, Task 1(f), and return-independent-hand-calculation-2.md, Q1(c); confirmed by both step-P1 readings (return-independent-hand-calculation-3.md and -4.md, Q3a).
rows.does_not_establish: It gives no rear-yard requirement for the part of the lot beyond 100 feet of the corner; that needs neighbouring lot-line data, the building type and lot width, and the ZR 12-10 lot-line definitions the earlier readers did not have (now captured and read in cases/step-p3-worked.json).

citations.title: Standard setback regulations
citations.quote: a setback with a depth of at least 10 feet shall be provided from any street wall fronting on a wide street, and a setback with a depth of at least 15 feet shall be provided from any street wall fronting on a narrow street

rows.why_applies: ZR 23-433 requires, between the minimum and maximum base heights, a setback of at least 10 feet from a street wall on a wide street and at least 15 feet on a narrow street. Northern Boulevard is wide and 215 Place is narrow.

expected.value: 10 ft on the wide street (Northern Boulevard); 15 ft on the narrow street (215 Place)

rows.source_reference: return-independent-hand-calculation-1.md, Task 1(d): '>=10 ft deep from any street wall on a WIDE street (Northern Blvd) and >=15 ft deep from any street wall on a NARROW street (215 Place)'.
rows.does_not_establish: The setback is not modelled on the lot here. Its depth may be reduced by one foot for each foot the street wall sits behind the street line, but not below seven feet (ZR 23-433(a)), and is optional under ZR 23-433(c).

citations.title: Rear yard requirements
citations.quote: shall be provided on #interior lots# in accordance with this Section

citations.title: Rear yard requirements
citations.quote: for #zoning lots# with a #lot width# of less than 40 feet, a #rear yard# with a depth of not less than 30 feet

rows.why_applies: The ordinary rear-yard depth for an interior lot is set by ZR 23-342 (now captured); it is not less than 20 feet or not less than 30 feet depending on the building type (detached or zero-lot-line, or semi-detached or attached) and the lot width (less than 40 feet, or 40 feet or greater).

expected.reason: ZR 23-342 is now captured, but the ordinary rear-yard depth it sets depends on the building type and the lot width, which are not given for this lot, so the depth is not known. Both step-P1 readings read the captured ZR 23-342 the same way (20 or 30 feet depending on building type and lot width, not given).

rows.source_reference: return-independent-hand-calculation-1.md, Task 1(f) and Task 3 item 4: 'ZR 23-342 is NOT in the packet; baseline depth NOT KNOWN from captured text'; with ZR 23-342 now captured, both step-P1 readings (return-independent-hand-calculation-3.md and -4.md, Q3) read the depth as 20 or 30 feet depending on building type and lot width, not given.
rows.does_not_establish: It gives no rear-yard depth for this lot; the captured ZR 23-342 sets 20 or 30 feet by building type and lot width, which are not given.
